title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Operations, and Top Support Fixes
author: Michael Rivera
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines standard operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation covering SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and canonical fixes for the top support issues. The goal is to keep user-facing developer docs accurate, discoverable, and low-support while enabling fast iteration by product and engineering teams.

Audience:
- SDK authors and maintainers
- Documentation engineers and content owners
- Developer support and solutions engineers
- Product and platform engineers publishing examples

Key objectives:
1) Provide consistent, tested SDK guides and quickstarts that get an engineer from zero to a working Redwood API call in < 10 minutes.
2) Maintain canonical API examples and code snippets across SDKs, CLI, and REST samples.
3) Operate a docs site with defined release, review, and rollback processes.
4) Reduce top-tier support tickets by documenting canonical fixes and triage flows.

Document structure (this page):
- Ownership and SLAs
- SDK guide standards
- Quickstarts & templates lifecycle
- API examples conventions and sync process
- Docs-site operating procedures (deploys, rollbacks, search index, analytics)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage + KB entry template)
- Checklists and runbooks

1. Ownership and SLAs

Owners:
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (Documentation team)
- SDK maintainers: each SDK repo has a code owner (see repo CODEOWNERS)
- Support triage: customer-success on first contact, escalate to Solutions/SDK owners for code issues

SLA targets:
- Documentation critical bug (broken example, missing auth): acknowledge within 4 business hours, fix or patch within 48 hours (hotfix branch + docs deploy).
- Minor doc edits / clarifications: update within 10 business days.
- SDK code example drift (failing CI/integration tests): patch or revert within 5 business days.

Escalation matrix:
1) Support engineer files a doc-issue in the docs repo and tags owner. If not acknowledged in 4 hours, page the Docs oncall.
2) If a public-production outage is involved, follow Incident Response playbook and snapshot docs changes separately for postmortem.

2. SDK guide standards

Standard sections for every SDK guide (order and headings are required):
- Quick summary (1-2 sentences)
- Prerequisites (SDK version, Node/Python/Go version, credentials, env vars)
- Installation (single-command install example)
- Authentication (example with API key and alternative with OAuth/KMS when applicable)
- Minimal working example (complete snippet that can be copy/pasted)
- Common patterns (streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings)
- Error handling and retries (with recommended backoff and SLOs)
- Troubleshooting (links to KB canonical fixes)
- API reference link and changelog pointer

Code hygiene and testing:
- All examples must be included in the SDK repo's examples/ directory and exercised by CI (unit and smoke tests).
- Example tests must run in the nightly docs CI matrix: node / python / go as applicable.
- Use the canonical API fixtures located in infra/docs-fixtures (contact docs infra owner for access).

Example minimal Node.js snippet (required in guide):
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', prompt: 'Write a haiku about dev docs' });
console.log(resp.output[0].text);

Authentication examples:
- API key (recommended for quickstarts): export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXX
- OAuth (enterprise flows): link to private-deployments/auth-guide

3. Quickstarts & templates lifecycle

Quickstart types:
- Interactive quickstarts (docs site + repl / live demo): targeted at new users.
- Repo templates (github templates for product teams): starter projects using Redwood hosted API or Dedicated configs.
- Internal engineering templates: canonical infra manifests and devcontainer setups for internal teams.

Template requirements:
- Each quickstart must include: README, LICENSE, CI workflow (tests + examples), minimal infra manifest (for dedicated/private quickstarts) and deployment notes.
- Version the quickstarts with a meta file quickstart.json containing fields: name, version, compatible_sdk_versions.

Release process for quickstarts / templates:
1) Author opens PR against docs/quickstarts with template and metadata.
2) Documentation review by Docs team (content) and SDK owner (code).
3) CI must pass for example tests and linting.
4) Merge and tag release; docs-site will pick up via docs CI.
5) Announce in #devex and add to quickstarts index page.

Deprecation policy:
- When removing a quickstart, mark as deprecated in the README and schedule removal 90 days later. Provide migration notes and automated codemod when feasible.

4. API examples conventions and sync process

Canonical examples:
- All REST/cURL and SDK examples must be single-source-of-truth in the examples/ directory of each SDK repo and referenced by docs via include snippets.
- Use the following canonical curl example pattern (must include explicit headers and sample body):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","prompt":"Hello from the canonical example","max_tokens":64}'

Snippet sync process:
1) Every docs CI run validates that examples in docs site match the files in SDK examples/ directory.
2) If mismatch detected, CI opens an automated PR against the docs site with the updated snippet and pings the owner.

Versioning and compatibility:
- Examples must include a compatibility badge (SDK version matrix) when APIs are subject to breaking changes.
- When rolling a breaking change, update the examples, add redirects, and preserve the last working version under /docs/v{major}/.

5. Docs-site operating procedures

CI / Deploy flow:
- Branch naming: docs/<team>-<short-desc>-YYYYMMDD (required)
- PR template must include: testing steps, snippets tested, and any infra changes
- Staging deploy: merges to main trigger staging build and automated smoke tests (link-checker, code snippet execution)
- Production deploy: weekly windows (Tuesdays 02:00-04:00 UTC) or ad-hoc for critical fixes (tagged hotfix).

Rollback procedure (step-by-step):
1) Identify the bad deploy and open a rollback ticket in the docs incident tracker.
2) Revert the merge commit and push; CI will trigger a staging build.
3) Confirm staging tests pass, then merge to main to release rollback.
4) Notify #docs and #devops with rollback summary and postmortem ETA.

Search & Analytics:
- Update search index after each production deploy.
- Docs analytics to track top failing snippets, time-to-first-successful-example, and support referral rate.
- Monthly dashboard owners: Docs lead and Developer Support manager.

Accessibility and localization:
- All public-facing quickstarts and SDK guides must meet WCAG 2.1 AA checks in the docs CI.
- Localization cadence: high-value pages (quickstarts, auth flows) prioritized quarterly.

6. Top support issues and canonical fixes

This section lists recurring developer support issues observed in the last 12 months and the canonical KB fix to include in docs and support scripts. Each entry uses the KB entry template below.

KB entry template (fields to include in every KB entry):
- Title
- Symptom (what the user sees)
- Root cause
- Fix (step-by-step)
- Workarounds if fix cannot be applied immediately
- Logs / diagnostic commands to collect
- Owner and urgency level

Most common issues (examples):
1) "401 / Invalid API key"
   - Symptom: API calls return 401 with "invalid_api_key"
   - Root cause: user set REDWOOD_API_KEY incorrectly (missing prefix or whitespace) or using expired key from the dashboard
   - Fix: Confirm key value, re-copy from Console > API Keys, export as: export REDWOOD_API_KEY='sk_live_xxx' and retry.
   - Diagnostics: curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status

2) "Streaming responses hang / incomplete chunked data"
   - Symptom: client hangs waiting for more tokens; partial output in logs
   - Root cause: network proxy or client not handling chunked transfer-encoding; some HTTP clients buffer by default.
   - Fix: Use official SDK streaming primitives (examples included below) or ensure HTTP client supports chunked responses and disables body buffering.
   - Diagnostics: curl --no-buffer -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" ...

3) "Model mismatch / incompatible request schema"
   - Symptom: 422 errors, or degraded output quality after model rollouts
   - Root cause: customer pinned to an older model variant or omitted required fields for new model weights
   - Fix: Share the model-compatibility table and recommend the correct request body. Include a migration snippet.

Sample KB entry (example fully formatted):
Title: CLI: "Rate limit exceeded" during bulk embed job
Symptom: 429 rate_limit_exceeded in logs while uploading 10k documents
Root cause: Default client concurrency and no backoff configured when using batching
Fix:
1) Throttle requests with exponential backoff; set concurrency to 5 and use batch size 64. Example pseudocode:
for batch in batches(docs, size=64):
  try:
    client.embeddings.create(batch)
  except RateLimitError:
    sleep(backoff.next())
    retry

2) For large workloads, use Redwood Dedicated with reserved throughput and the bulk upload API.
Diagnostics: attach request_id header values and example payload sizes.
Owner: Solutions Engineering (priority: medium)

7. Checklists and runbooks

Pre-merge checklist for doc PRs:
- [ ] Includes required headings and minimal copy
- [ ] Examples live in SDK repo and are referenced by file path
- [ ] CI examples/tests passed in staging matrix
- [ ] Accessibility checks green
- [ ] Owner review completed and approvals recorded

Hotfix runbook (critical broken example or auth issue):
1) Triage and create docs-hotfix branch with minimal revert or patch.
2) Run smoke tests locally and in CI.
3) Merge and trigger production hotfix deploy.
4) Post to #docs and #support with rollback plan.
5) Create postmortem if incident impacted production customers.

Maintenance cadence:
- Weekly: Docs triage meeting (15 min) to review new issues and CI failures.
- Monthly: Cleanup orphaned examples and validate quickstart CI.
- Quarterly: Audit top-20 pages and run user testing on quickstarts.

Appendix: Useful commands and links
- Run local docs server: ./scripts/docs-dev --port 3000
- Validate snippets: ./scripts/validate-snippets.sh
- Rebuild search index: ./scripts/reindex-search.sh --env production
- Docs CI status: https://ci.internal.redwood/docs (internal)
- SDK examples index: https://git.internal.redwood.com/redwood-sdk-examples (internal)

Contact and governance
- Docs lead: Michael Rivera (mrivera@redwood.ai)
- Doc infra owner: Priya Natarajan (pnatarajan@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: #docs and #dev-support in Slack

This playbook should be reviewed at least annually or after any major docs-site/platform change (search index changes, new snippet runner, or major SDK release).
